A2.text:
Nargiz is twenty-one. Next week she has her first job interview at a design studio in Baku. She wanted to dress to impress, so on Saturday morning she went to the big mall with her friend Lala.

Every shop window had the same autumn trend: short beige jackets. Nargiz tried one off the rack, but the fit was terrible on her shoulders. Also, the famous brand was much too expensive for a student.

When she came home in the evening, she was sad. Her mother opened the old wooden wardrobe in the hallway. Inside was a long dark-green wool coat. “It was mine in 1998,” her mother said warmly. “Try it on.”

At first, Nargiz did not want a hand-me-down for such an important day. Then she looked in the mirror. With a simple silk scarf as an accessory, the whole outfit looked wonderful.

On Monday, six other girls waited at the studio. Five of them wore the same beige jacket from the mall. When Nargiz walked into the room, the manager smiled at her coat. “That colour is always in fashion,” she said. “And we love sustainable fashion here.”

Nargiz got the job — and she never bought the beige jacket.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A girl who wears her mother's old green coat to an interview and stands out from the crowd
How to open a clothes shop in a Baku mall
Why beige jackets are the best clothes for work
A mother who works at a design studio
questions.why: Instead of buying the trendy beige jacket everyone else wears, Nargiz wears her mother's 1998 coat and gets the job.

questions.q: What was wrong with the beige jacket at the mall?
options: It was dirty
The fit was bad on her shoulders and the brand was too expensive
They did not have her colour
Lala bought the last one
questions.why: “The fit was terrible on her shoulders. Also, the famous brand was much too expensive.”

questions.q: What accessory did Nargiz wear with the green coat?
options: A gold watch
A leather hat
A simple silk scarf
A big red bag
questions.why: “With a simple silk scarf as an accessory, the whole outfit looked wonderful.”

questions.q: Nargiz was the only person at the interview wearing the beige jacket.
options: True
False
Not given
questions.why: Five of the other girls wore the beige jacket, while Nargiz wore the green coat.

questions.q: At first, Nargiz did not want a “hand-me-down”. What is a “hand-me-down”?
options: A very expensive new dress
A piece of clothing passed from an older person in the family
A uniform for work
A coat made of rainproof plastic
questions.why: It was her mother's coat from 1998 that her mother gave to her.

questions.q: Why was the manager pleased when she saw Nargiz's coat?
options: She had the same beige jacket at home
It showed personal style and fitted the studio's love of sustainable fashion
She knew Nargiz's mother
Green was the company's official uniform
questions.why: Unlike the five identical jackets, the vintage coat had character and matched their sustainable values.

B1.text:
When Nargiz was invited to interview at a small architecture and design studio in Baku, her first thought was that she had nothing suitable to wear. She wanted to dress to impress, so she spent Saturday afternoon walking from floor to floor through the mall with her best friend Lala.

Every shop window showed the same autumn trend: boxy beige blazers. Nargiz pulled three of them off the rack, but on her narrow shoulders the fit was all wrong, and the price tag on even an ordinary brand made her wince. After two hours, she came home tired and empty-handed.

Her mother listened quietly, then opened the back of the hallway wardrobe and lifted out a dark-green wool coat with brass buttons. “I bought this in Tbilisi in 1998,” she said. “An old tailor near the theatre adjusted the sleeves for me.”

Nargiz hesitated; turning up to a design interview in a family hand-me-down felt risky. Then she put it on in front of the mirror. The heavy wool fell cleanly, and when she added her grandmother's patterned silk scarf as a single accessory, the whole outfit looked as if it had been made for her alone.

On Monday morning, six candidates sat in the studio reception. Four of them were wearing the exact same beige blazer from the mall. When Nargiz was called in, the creative director noticed the green coat at once. “Proper tailoring is always in fashion,” she said warmly. “And we care a lot about sustainable fashion in our work — reusing good things instead of buying ten disposable ones.”

Walking home with the job offer in her bag, Nargiz stopped by the tailor's shop on her street — not to buy anything new, just to have the brass buttons polished.

questions.q: What lesson does Nargiz's experience suggest about style?
options: You must always buy the newest clothes for an interview
Well-made clothes with personal history make a stronger impression than copying a fast trend
Design studios only hire people who wear green
Tailors in Tbilisi are better than shops in Baku
questions.why: Four candidates wear the same mall blazer, while Nargiz's tailored 1998 coat wins the creative director's respect.

questions.q: Where had Nargiz's mother originally bought the green coat?
options: In a Baku mall
In Tbilisi in 1998
Online last winter
From the creative director
questions.why: “I bought this in Tbilisi in 1998,” she said.

questions.q: What did Nargiz see when she arrived in the studio reception?
options: Nobody else had come
Four of the six candidates were wearing the same beige blazer from the mall
Everyone was wearing dark green
Her friend was also waiting there
questions.why: “Four of them were wearing the exact same beige blazer from the mall.”

questions.q: The creative director asked Nargiz where she could buy the same coat.
options: True
False
Not given
questions.why: She praises the tailoring and sustainable fashion, but never asks where to buy one.

questions.q: Nargiz pulled three blazers “off the rack”. What does “off the rack” mean?
options: Made by a tailor for one person
Ready-made in standard sizes in a shop
From the top shelf at home
Borrowed from a friend
questions.why: They were ready-made shop blazers, unlike her mother's coat whose sleeves a tailor had adjusted.

questions.q: Why does Nargiz visit the tailor on the way home?
options: To make the coat shorter
To return the coat to its owner
Because she now values taking care of a lasting piece of clothing
Because a button fell off during the interview
questions.why: Instead of shopping for something new, she wants the brass buttons on the 1998 coat polished.

B2.text:
When twenty-one-year-old Nargiz was shortlisted for a junior role at a respected Baku interior studio, she assumed her first task was to dress to impress. Saturday afternoon therefore found her standing in the harsh white light of a mall changing room, surrounded by the season's inescapable trend: oversized oatmeal blazers that promised effortless authority to anyone willing to pay for them.

She tried five of them off the rack. Every single one drowned her narrow shoulders; the fabric felt suspiciously like recycled plastic, and the price demanded by even a mid-range brand was enough to make a recent graduate laugh bitterly. After three hours of identical rails, she went home empty-handed and quietly discouraged.

Her mother listened at the kitchen table without comment, then unlocked the cedar wardrobe in the corridor and lifted out a deep moss-green coat cut from heavy wool. “Tbilisi, November 1998,” she said, brushing the lapel with her hand. “An old tailor near the dry bridge altered the shoulders for me before my first teaching job.”

Nargiz was initially reluctant to attend the most important meeting of her life in a family hand-me-down. Yet the moment she buttoned it in front of the hall mirror, the difference between assembly-line cloth and a garment with bones was unmistakable: the fit was clean, calm and deliberate. Paired with her grandmother's narrow silk scarf as the sole accessory, the outfit looked quietly self-assured.

On Monday morning, five other applicants sat in the studio waiting room, four of them in identical oatmeal blazers from the mall. When Nargiz walked into the interview room, the studio's founder glanced at the coat and smiled. “Good wool never goes out of style — it is always in fashion,” she remarked. “We spend half our time persuading clients to choose materials that age well; sustainable fashion and sustainable rooms obey the exact same rule.”

That evening, with the contract signed in her bag, Nargiz took the coat to the small tailor on her street — not to change a single line of it, only to have the silk lining steamed for its next twenty years.

words.tr: ön elemeyi geçti / kısa listeye kaldı

questions.q: What parallel does the story draw between clothing and the studio's design work?
options: Both should be changed every season to follow trends
Both are best when made from lasting materials with honest craftsmanship rather than disposable trends
Both must be imported from abroad
Both are too expensive for young graduates
questions.why: The founder notes that “sustainable fashion and sustainable rooms obey the same rule”: choosing materials that age well.

questions.q: Why did Nargiz leave the mall without buying a blazer?
options: The shops had closed early
The blazers drowned her shoulders, felt synthetic and cost too much
She forgot her bank card
Her mother called her to come home
questions.why: “Every single one drowned her shoulders; the fabric felt like recycled plastic, and the price... was enough to make a graduate laugh.”

questions.q: Who had altered the shoulders of the green coat in 1998?
options: Nargiz's grandmother
An old tailor near the dry bridge in Tbilisi
The founder of the Baku studio
A shop assistant at the mall
questions.why: “An old tailor near the dry bridge altered the shoulders for me.”

questions.q: Nargiz asked the tailor on her street to shorten the coat after she got the job.
options: True
False
Not given
questions.why: She took it “not to change a line of it, only to have the lining steamed”.

questions.q: Nargiz assumed her first task was to “dress to impress”. What does this mean?
options: Wear the most comfortable clothes she owned
Wear clothes chosen to make people admire and respect her
Design a new uniform for the studio
Spend as little money as possible
questions.why: She wanted her clothes for the interview to give her “effortless authority” and make a strong first impression.

questions.q: What does the phrase “a garment with bones” suggest about the green coat?
options: It was stiff and uncomfortable to wear
It had real structure and tailoring, unlike the shapeless mall blazers
It was too heavy for Baku weather
It had bone buttons
questions.why: It is contrasted with “assembly-line cloth”, and the next clause says “the fit was clean and deliberate”.
